{"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"Decoupling these components increases modularity and maintainability. Each engine has a clear responsibility and communicates through well-defined interfaces."},{"type":"ui","source":"root = Stack([definition,diagram,summary])
definition = Text("""The Conversation Engine manages messages and their lineage, storing user and system exchanges. The Context Engine selects relevant references and manages context budgets, ensuring only necessary information is passed to the Conversation Engine. The Application Orchestrator coordinates the flow, triggering context selection and message updates as needed.""")
diagram = Graphic("Engine Relationships", [group([rect(30,20,110,40),text(35,35,"Conversation Engine")]), group([rect(170,20,110,40),text(175,35,"Context Engine")]), group([rect(90,80,110,40),text(95,95,"App Orchestrator")]), path("M140 40 L170 40"), path("M110 60 L110 80"), path("M220 60 L145 80")])
summary = Text("""- The Conversation Engine exposes methods to add, retrieve, and trace messages.
- The Context Engine exposes methods to select and budget references, returning only what the Conversation Engine needs.
- The Application Orchestrator listens for user actions, invokes the Context Engine to select context, then updates the Conversation Engine with new messages and lineage.
- Communication is via interfaces (e.g., function calls, events, or APIs), not direct data sharing.
- Each engine can be replaced or updated independently as long as interfaces remain stable.""")","state":[]}]}

At most one ui block contains only the requested protocol source and initial integer state entries (empty uses defaults). No fences. No JavaScript, tools, events, HTML or links. One Stack with unique named leaves. Up to 40 leaves, 40 collection members, 64 declarations, depth 32, 16000 UTF-8 source bytes, 10000 frame bytes. Integers for input state. Names start with ASCII letter, then alphanumeric or underscore, at most 48 characters. All declarations must be reachable. Text and labels at most 512 characters. Safe Graphic items use kind plus only required fields: rect(x,y,width,height), circle(cx,cy,r), text(x,y,text), path(d using only M L H V Z, lowercase equivalents, numbers, spaces or commas), group(items of leaves). Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
One assignment per physical line. root = Stack([leafName, otherLeaf]). Each leaf is one named call: Text("text"), Metric("label",numericValue), Control("label",literalMin,literalMax,choices,$variable), Table([{label:"name",score:number}]), Graphic("label",items). Declare $variable = integer and bind it to exactly one Control. Use [] for range or literal string options indexed 0..n-1. Derived name = expression. Strings use double quotes. Numeric + - * /, == > <, condition ? yes : no, arrays, objects, named references, @Sum(numbers), @Sort(rows,"score","desc") are allowed. No unary minus, concatenation, member access, map, interpolation or inline nested components. Produce complete root and definitions.
Choose text for a simple definition. Use a legible diagram if spatial relationships aid understanding. Use controls for a changing decision. Label units, state assumptions, use short readable labels, give each output an informative name and check zero or boundary conditions. Keep geometry inside the viewBox.
Treat the request as the complete source of domain rules. Include exactly its input dimensions, options, units, defaults and ranges. Check that each input changes the intended outputs. Do not invent extra tiers, exceptions or fees. Interpret terminology in its application context. Provide an actual interaction when requested. Do not claim a visible control exists in prose alone.
Unrelated response-shape examples. Derive the actual content from the user request.

{"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"Decoupling a Conversation Engine, Context Engine, and Application Orchestrator means each has a single responsibility and interacts through clear interfaces. This improves modularity, testability, and maintainability."},{"type":"ui","source":"root = Stack([definition,diagram,steps])
definition = Text("""- The Conversation Engine owns messages and their lineage (history and relationships).
- The Context Engine selects relevant references and manages context budgets (limits on information passed).
- The Application Orchestrator coordinates both, managing the flow of information and operations.""")
diagram = Graphic("Engine Decoupling Diagram", [rect(30,20,120,40), text(35,35,"Conversation Engine"), rect(180,20,120,40), text(185,35,"Context Engine"), rect(90,80,120,40), text(95,95,"App Orchestrator"), path("M150 40 L180 40"), path("M120 60 L120 80"), path("M240 60 L150 80")])
steps = Text("""1. The Application Orchestrator receives user input or triggers.
2. It asks the Context Engine to select and budget references.
3. It passes these to the Conversation Engine, which updates messages and lineage.
4. Each engine exposes only necessary interfaces (e.g., APIs, function calls).
5. No engine directly accesses another's internal data; all communication is explicit.""")","state":[]}]}
